old: but that very uniqueness, her trace of education
new: but the very things that set her apart, her trace of education
reason: Right after 'not unique or even infrequent', 'that very uniqueness' sounds self-contradictory to a listener.

old: "I'll become one myself soon! It's contagious!"
new: "I'll become one myself soon! It's contagious!" he thought.
reason: The line has no speaker tag, so a listener cannot tell that it is Raskolnikov's private thought rather than something Sonia says aloud.

new: Katerina Ivanovna is mad and consumptive
reason: Coming right after 'if you're really taken to the hospital', 'She' could be heard as Sonia herself.
A short gloss helps a listener with the French phrase, which comes up again in the next paragraph.

new: the old Austrian war council, the _Hofkriegsrath_
reason: The German term is opaque when heard, and 'war council' lets the Napoleon and General Mack joke land.

old: don't consider that 'when they overstep all obstacles,' as you put it so wittily yesterday.
new: don't take that into account when they 'overstep all obstacles,' as you put it so wittily yesterday.
reason: As written, the sentence breaks off: 'don't consider that' leads into a clause that is never finished, so it sounds ungrammatical.

old: Dmitri Prokofitch came to see me yesterday
new: Dmitri Prokofitch—Razumihin—came to see me yesterday
reason: The edition usually calls him Razumihin, so a listener may not recognise him by his first name and patronymic (the exchange about him continues in 25.55 and 25.63).

old: what good is that fat fellow?
new: what good is that fat doctor of yours?
reason: Nothing nearby says who 'that fat fellow' is; calling him a doctor identifies Raskolnikov's physician.
